Medicinal uses of Cannabis

By: Eugene Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
.....why some say Cannabis is realy, really good for you

Summary:
There is currently a raging debate around the medicinal used of cannabis in South Africa, sparked by a conference held in Benoni this week. It harks back to the campaign started by Mario Ambrosini that really went nowhere.

The debate in South Africa can benefit by insights from the US where the conversation has been ongoing for many years and where it is slightly more sophisticated. In the US 23 states have allowed the medicinal use of cannabis and 3 states so far have approved the recreational use of cannabis.

There is a story behind the story -- why was cannabis outlawed in the US? Could it have been for other than medical reasons? Dr David Bearman, one of the US's foremost practitioners prescribing cannabis to patients believes that this is the case. He is a passionate supporter of the medicinal use of cannabis and has recently also published a book "Drugs are NOT the Tools of the Devil: How Discrimination and Greed Created a Dysfunctional Drug Policy and How It Can Be Fixed". He considers cannabis a wonder drug that is non-toxic and has a plethora of medicinal uses, including fighting cancer. And he says it has no side effects.

Dr Donald P. Tashkin is an American pulmonologist at UCLA who has studied the effects of cannabis Tashkin has spent 30 years studying cannabis. In 2006, he was in charge of a large case-control study on marijuana and the risk of cancer. Contrary to his group's expectations, the study found no increase in lung cancer risk even among heavy users of marijuana. We met him and it is surprising to find that he, as medical specialist, considers cannabis smoking beneficial for general lung health.

We have interviews with both these specialists, and they have surprising medical insights and claims -- contrary to what is commonly believed about cannabis..

• Remove Quintin completely
• Put in Ambrosini speaking from our footage – very moving.

Use Derek in links to say these things so that its clear that we are neutral.
• End in a way that is more open ended, and saying we think that this should be considered and research is ongoing.

Press Release:


Medical Marijuana
Could a single plant-based substance have enough significant therapeutic properties to offer relief to people with multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, cancers, asthma, migraines, post-traumatic stress disorders and more? Top American scientists and people cured of cancers bring controversial claims to the fore as Carte Blanche investigates the medicinal use of Marijuana.


Script:


Dr Bearman:
If you have attention deficit disorder, you can’t focus, it’s going to help you do your homework better. If you have post-traumatic stress disorder it’s going to make you more comfortable in your own skin. You are not going to have so much easy startle, the nightmares are going to go away.

Dr Tashkin:
It has a suppressant effect on a variety of cancers…not only lung, but also breast, prostate, etcetera.

DEREK LINK:
These two American specialists are referring to a single drug that has all these amazing effects. And there are indications that this drug is also effective for epilepsy, multiple sclerosis, glaucoma, migraines and asthma.
V/O:
Dr David Bearman, based in Santa Barbara in California, says he first heard about this wonder drug about 40 years ago.
Dr Bearman:
It was too much of a good thing. I figured they got to be pulling my leg. How could anything do all these things? Well, it can.

V/O:
This seemingly amazing drug is prepared from this plant – Cannabis Sativa and is also known as marijuana or dagga in South Africa.Dr Bearman is one of the leading physicians in the US in the field of Medical Marijuana and has recently published a book on drugs and drug policies. He says despite marijuana’s reputation, there is scientific evidence that it is effective against some cancers.

Kim:
I am 100% healthy. I was given 2 weeks to 2 months in July last year. I am 100% cured.

V/O:
Eight years ago Kim Collins of Kwazulu Natal beat cancer, but last year a large malignant tumour was discovered in her liver. She was immediately put on aggressive chemo therapy to shrink the tumour so that it could be removed surgically.

Derek Link:
After three months of chemo the tumour had only shrunk by 5%. Kim’s oncologist ordered another 6 months of chemo therapy.
V/O:
Kim was not willing to continue the ordeal and was only given a few months to live.But her son insisted that she try cannabis as a last resort. Reluctantly she followed his advice and a herbalist prescribed taking the equivalent of the volume of one rice grain of concentrated cannabis oil. at a time

Derek:
Kim, in what form is this cannabis oil when you take it?

Kim:
This is actually what it looks like, Derek. It is a little syringe and this is how much one rice grain is. So what you do is you take one rice grain and one teaspoon of coconut oil. You mix it together and what you do is you out your finger in and you rub it in your gums like that, and that’s it.

V/O:
The Cannabis oil had an almost immediate effect on Kim.

Kim:
It did make all my anxiety go away. I was much calmer. And it took a lot of the ain away.

V/O:
After three months on only cannabis oil Kim had another scan and received amazing news: the tumour had begun to die and could be removed. She is now cancer free.

DEREK LINK:
Cannabis oil in a syringe of this size, sells for between R500 and R3500. Expensive, but cheap compared to conventional cancer treatments.

V/O:
Cannabis has such a profound effect on a variety of conditions because of a network in the human body called the endocannabinoid system. It was first discovered in the nineteen eighties and it consists of a huge number of receptors in the brain and throughout the body that interact with chemical compounds called cannabinoids.These cannabinoids affect the release of neurotransmitters and can slow down the rate of electrical impulses in the brain and nervous system. And this impacts a large number of physiological processes in the brain and human body.
Our bodies themselves manufacture these cannabinoids, BUT researchers have also identified about 85 cannabinoids in the cannabis plant. These cannabinoids are freely accepted by the body’s cannabinoid receptors. And they too have a huge influence on a variety physical and biochemical functions of cells and organs. For example, a well-known cannabinoid, THC, specifically slows down electrical impulses in the brain.
Dr. Bearman
Well you can see if you have a migraine headache or a seizure, each of which is caused by excessive electrical stimulation, excessive neural stimulation that if you slow down the speed of neural impulses you are going to slow down the amount of neural stimulation and therefore you might prevent the migraine or make it less severe and the same thing with the seizure. You may prevent it or make it less severe.

LINK:
THC’s also cause the release of large amounts of dopamine in the brain and this explains the euphoric and relaxing effect of cannabis.

V/O:
Dr Bearman says many scientific studies done over the years have begun to dispel some long-held erroneous beliefs about cannabis. One being that it causes brain damage.

Bearman:
Where that comes from is from a particularly bad piece of research done by a drug warrior zealot, done back in the seventies.

V/O:
This researcher put a gas mask on lab monkeys and pumped it full of cannabis smoke with virtually no oxygen. The monkeys developed brain damage.

Bearman:
Now what we know from real research is that Cannabis is neuroprotective. It actually makes your brain cells live longer.

V/O:
And Dr Bearman says cannabis is not addictive.

Bearman:
It is not addictive. Can dependence occur with Cannabis? Absolutely. How serious is this? Not as serious as dependence on coffee. People say “Oh, you mean it is not serious?” Have you ever seen anybody who has dependence on coffee? It can be serious. But it is not addiction. Most people who use marijuana use it for a few years and stop. Voluntarily. No withdrawal symptoms.

V/O:
This is a controversial opinion and many mainstream academics and scientists have the opposite view. However, research done at the University of California found that smoking cannabis or marijuana is not harmful to the lungs. Dr Donald Tashkin is a pulmonologist who led a major study on lung function and cannabis smoking.

Dr Tashkin:
Marijuana smokers had essentially normal lung function. There was no evidence of any abnormality that would suggest airflow obstruction.

V/O:
Both Dr Tashkin and Bearman say that contrary to popular belief, science has proven that cannabis is not a gateway drug at all.

Bearman:
The use of cannabis does not lead to the use of other drugs. Anybody who knows anything about science and the brain and substance abuse realizes that that statement is absurd it is only used for propaganda purposes.

Dr Tashkin:
It is true that crack users also tend to use other substances like marijuana, but that may be due to their underlying personalities or environmental influences rather than marijuana itself predisposing by some chemical or pharmacological means to the use of other substances.

DEREK LINK:
However, various researchers have pointed out that that because cannabis is psycho-active, it can has side effects such as intensifying existing psychoses. And there are others.

Dr Bearman
If you had a high dose and you were a naïve user, you might become anxious, you might become paranoid, and you might even have a panic attack. Those things are not likely, they do no happen often but they do happen.

V/O:
The therapeutic value of cannabis was recognized millennia ago with cannabis extracts widely used by physicians in ancient China, India and Rome. It was also extremely popular in Europe and the US in the 19th century.

Dr Bearman:
At the turn of the 19th to the 20th century it was the third most used therapeutic medication in the United States after alcohol and opium. It was found in many medicines, doctors wrote prescriptions for it. As late as the 1920’s American physicians wrote three million prescriptions a year that contained cannabis.

V/O:
But despite its benefits cannabis was banned in the USA. It was also banned in South Africa in 1928, where propaganda demonized it and depicted it as evil.

UPSOUND: REEFER MADNESS FILM

Only very recently, and based on what science has begun to reveal about it, has marijuana again been legalized for medicinal purposes in 24 states in the US.

V/O:
In South Africa the legalization of cannabis for medicinal use is also on the agenda. Several individuals and lobby groups have been petitioning Government for this. In February 2014, terminally ill IFP Parliamentarian Mario Ambrosini, tabled a private members bill on Medical Innovation in an attempt to legalise use of cannabinoids for medical purposes.

Ambrosini:
There is no rational argument for continuing to deprive medical marijuana to people like who need it.

LINK:
The Bill lapsed when he died, but there are initiatives underway in Parliament to re-introduce the Bill.

V/O:
And in March this year the Government organized a Cannabis Round table through the Central Drug Authority. Janet O’Donoghue, an activist for medicinal cannabis, was there.

Janet:
The purpose of the Cannabis Round Table was for them to prepare a position paper to present to Parliament, the Health Committee. It was attended by a hundred or so people. The central theme of the roundtable was Medical Cannabis or Cannabis for medical use – yes or no. That was the question that was asked.

V/O:
Following this meeting, a report is now being compiled and many believe legalization is imminent. Organizations like Janet’s are engaging Government on this.
Janet:
We are proposing to the Government a means for them to legitimately, peacefully and successfully roll out legal cannabis in South Africa.

V/O:
But for the moment, in South Africa any possession of cannabis in any form is illegal – even for medicinal use and even if it could save lives.

Greg Wooley is the herbalist in Durban who assisted Kim with cannabis oil to treat her cancer. But by supplying Kim with cannabis oil Greg was breaking South African law and he was arrested.

Derek:
What were you charged with?

Greg:
I’ve been charged with possession and trafficking. Merely because I cooperated and said I was giving it to some patients. So they decided to put the trafficking on it as well.

V/O:
Greg says his experience with Kim’s cancer has proven to him that the battle to legalize medicinal cannabis is worth it.

Greg:
When that kind of result comes through, you fall off your chair. It is the thrill, Derek, of seeing hope coming to people’s eyes where there was none.

V/O: Dr Bearman says many scientific studies done over the years have begun to dispel some long-held erroneous beliefs about cannabis. One being that it causes brain damage. Bearman: Where that comes from is from a particularly bad piece of research done by a drug warrior zealot, done back in the seventies. V/O: This researcher put a gas mask on lab monkeys and pumped it full of cannabis smoke with virtually no oxygen. The monkeys developed brain damage. Bearman: Now what we know from real research is that Cannabis is neuroprotective. It actually makes your brain cells live longer. V/O: And Dr Bearman says cannabis is not addictive. Bearman: It is not addictive. Can dependence occur with Cannabis? Absolutely. How serious is this? Not as serious as dependence on coffee. People say “Oh, you mean it is not serious?” Have you ever seen anybody who has dependence on coffee? It can be serious. But it is not addiction. Most people who use marijuana use it for a few years and stop. Voluntarily. No withdrawal symptoms. V/O: This is a controversial opinion and many mainstream academics and scientists have the opposite view. However, research done at the University of California found that smoking cannabis or marijuana is not harmful to the lungs. Dr Donald Tashkin is a pulmonologist who led a major study on lung function and cannabis smoking. Dr Tashkin: Marijuana smokers had essentially normal lung function. There was no evidence of any abnormality that would suggest airflow obstruction. V/O: Both Dr Tashkin and Bearman say that contrary to popular belief, science has proven that cannabis is not a gateway drug at all. Bearman: The use of cannabis does not lead to the use of other drugs. Anybody who knows anything about science and the brain and substance abuse realizes that that statement is absurd it is only used for propaganda purposes. Dr Tashkin: It is true that crack users also tend to use other substances like marijuana, but that may be due to their underlying personalities or environmental influences rather than marijuana itself predisposing by some chemical or pharmacological means to the use of other substances. DEREK LINK: However, various researchers have pointed out that that because cannabis is psycho-active, it can has side effects such as intensifying existing psychoses. And there are others. Dr Bearman If you had a high dose and you were a naïve user, you might become anxious, you might become paranoid, and you might even have a panic attack. Those things are not likely, they do no happen often but they do happen. V/O: The therapeutic value of cannabis was recognized millennia ago with cannabis extracts widely used by physicians in ancient China, India and Rome. It was also extremely popular in Europe and the US in the 19th century. Dr Bearman: At the turn of the 19th to the 20th century it was the third most used therapeutic medication in the United States after alcohol and opium. It was found in many medicines, doctors wrote prescriptions for it. As late as the 1920’s American physicians wrote three million prescriptions a year that contained cannabis. V/O: But despite its benefits cannabis was banned in the USA. It was also banned in South Africa in 1928, where propaganda demonized it and depicted it as evil. UPSOUND: REEFER MADNESS FILM Only very recently, and based on what science has begun to reveal about it, has marijuana again been legalized for medicinal purposes in 24 states in the US. V/O: In South Africa the legalization of cannabis for medicinal use is also on the agenda. Several individuals and lobby groups have been petitioning Government for this. In February 2014, terminally ill IFP Parliamentarian Mario Ambrosini, tabled a private members bill on Medical Innovation in an attempt to legalise use of cannabinoids for medical purposes. Ambrosini: There is no rational argument for continuing to deprive medical marijuana to people like who need it. LINK: The Bill lapsed when he died, but there are initiatives underway in Parliament to re-introduce the Bill. V/O: And in March this year the Government organized a Cannabis Round table through the Central Drug Authority. Janet O’Donoghue, an activist for medicinal cannabis, was there. Janet: The purpose of the Cannabis Round Table was for them to prepare a position paper to present to Parliament, the Health Committee. It was attended by a hundred or so people. The central theme of the roundtable was Medical Cannabis or Cannabis for medical use – yes or no. That was the question that was asked. V/O: Following this meeting, a report is now being compiled and many believe legalization is imminent. Organizations like Janet’s are engaging Government on this. Janet: We are proposing to the Government a means for them to legitimately, peacefully and successfully roll out legal cannabis in South Africa. V/O: But for the moment, in South Africa any possession of cannabis in any form is illegal – even for medicinal use and even if it could save lives. Greg Wooley is the herbalist in Durban who assisted Kim with cannabis oil to treat her cancer. But by supplying Kim with cannabis oil Greg was breaking South African law and he was arrested. Derek: What were you charged with? Greg: I’ve been charged with possession and trafficking. Merely because I cooperated and said I was giving it to some patients. So they decided to put the trafficking on it as well. V/O: Greg says his experience with Kim’s cancer has proven to him that the battle to legalize medicinal cannabis is worth it. Greg: When that kind of result comes through, you fall off your chair. It is the thrill, Derek, of seeing hope coming to people’s eyes where there was none. metadata.Summary: There is currently a raging debate around the medicinal used of cannabis in South Africa, sparked by a conference held in Benoni this week. It harks back to the campaign started by Mario Ambrosini that really went nowhere. The debate in South Africa can benefit by insights from the US where the conversation has been ongoing for many years and where it is slightly more sophisticated. In the US 23 states have allowed the medicinal use of cannabis and 3 states so far have approved the recreational use of cannabis. There is a story behind the story -- why was cannabis outlawed in the US? Could it have been for other than medical reasons? Dr David Bearman, one of the US's foremost practitioners prescribing cannabis to patients believes that this is the case. He is a passionate supporter of the medicinal use of cannabis and has recently also published a book "Drugs are NOT the Tools of the Devil: How Discrimination and Greed Created a Dysfunctional Drug Policy and How It Can Be Fixed". He considers cannabis a wonder drug that is non-toxic and has a plethora of medicinal uses, including fighting cancer. And he says it has no side effects. Dr Donald P. Tashkin is an American pulmonologist at UCLA who has studied the effects of cannabis Tashkin has spent 30 years studying cannabis. In 2006, he was in charge of a large case-control study on marijuana and the risk of cancer. Contrary to his group's expectations, the study found no increase in lung cancer risk even among heavy users of marijuana. We met him and it is surprising to find that he, as medical specialist, considers cannabis smoking beneficial for general lung health. We have interviews with both these specialists, and they have surprising medical insights and claims -- contrary to what is commonly believed about cannabis..
